claims.text: Tailored thermo-mechanical processing can transform as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 into an ultrafine duplex microstructure that inherits eutectic lamellae.
The ultrafine duplex lamellar microstructure simultaneously improves strength and ductility.
The initial AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy has an as-cast, relatively coarse eutectic microstructure.
The tailored thermo-mechanical process specifically consists of severe plastic deformation by rolling followed by controlled annealing.
Optimizing rolling intensity and annealing temperature and time promotes phase decomposition and formation of a hierarchical duplex lamellar structure.
The resulting microstructure provides a two-hierarchical constraint effect.
The resulting microstructure activates a self-generated microcrack-arresting mechanism.
Processing increases the density of interfaces and grain boundaries.
The increased interface and grain-boundary density impedes dislocation motion and thereby increases strength.
The inherited lamellar architecture permits controlled plasticity.
The inherited lamellar architecture arrests microcracks and thereby improves ductility.
Relative to the as-cast alloy, the processed alloy will show statistically significant increases in both yield strength and ductility.
Yield strength is anticipated to increase by approximately 20–30% relative to the as-cast baseline.
Ductility is anticipated to improve by a similar relative amount of approximately 20–30%.
The hypothesis should extend to eutectic high-entropy alloys having compositions and casting conditions similar to AlCoCrFeNi2.1.
Changes in composition, cooling rate, deformation level, or annealing conditions may prevent formation of the desired duplex microstructure and alter the mechanical properties.
